mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when GDP is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions, which historically correlate with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts and retail sales signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when both housing starts and retail sales are increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales over two consecutive months signals a strong consumer demand, which typically boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when retail sales are increasing.
